chapter: Stuff Smith stories, Wes Montgomery and singers
title: The string album with Wes Montgomery and Kenny Burrell
summary: A string date with two guitars, Hank Jones and Milt Hinton; Wes turned his music upside down and the strings tapped bows for him.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: When was the first time you worked with Wes?
Oh, boy, let me see. We did a string album, and I said, well, the people that I want -- I wanted two guitarists so I got Kenny Burrell.
There was a duet, you know. They worked out beautifully. I had some of the best string players out of New York. I had Dick Hyman and Hank Jones on piano. Ossie Johnson and Milt Hinton, you know.
Gloria Agostini on harp. It was a very successful thing.
And Wes was funny. He used to come -- you know, he didn't read. In fact he didn't have to read. He was something like Erroll Garner, why should he read when he can play like that.
So Wes would come in and turn his music upside down.
And he cracked all the fiddle players up, you know?

But when he would finish a solo they would give him what they call the bow tap, you know, that's applause. Because the neck of the guitar is related like to the neck of a violin. And he was doing some phenomenal things on it, you know?
